os_overview.title: Company OS: your business computer
lines: The Overview shows today's numbers: cash, money waiting at ShopLane, orders to pack.
Use the tabs on the left. Every laptop and work desk opens the same system: home, co-work hot desk, café table, office.
The clock keeps running while you're at the computer, just like in real life. Buying, listing and working also take their own time.

os_operations.title: Operations: buying stock
lines: Suppliers sell in minimum order quantities (MOQ). You pay up front and the stock arrives in a few days (ARRIVES shows when).
Stock is delivered to where you work: home holds 600 units, an office holds more.
Buy what sells: Sales shows the expected orders per day before you buy more.

os_sales.title: Sales: listings on ShopLane
lines: List a product you have in stock. Shoot the photos yourself (a photo shoot you play) or pay Studio Lumen $120 for pro photos.
Set the price with − and +. Expected orders per day update as you change it: cheaper sells more but earns less per sale.
Ads buy more views for a daily budget. ShopLane takes a 10% fee and pays out every Monday.

os_inventory.title: Inventory: what you have and where
lines: Units on hand at each location, units reserved for orders, and units on the way.
Everything you store takes space at that location.

os_finance.title: Finance: profit is not cash
lines: Profit and loss shows what you earned this month. The cash forecast shows when money actually comes in and goes out.
Sales money waits at ShopLane before it reaches your bank. Big invoices on long terms can leave you short of cash even when you are profitable.

os_people.title: People: hiring staff
lines: First register as an employer at City Hall (the permits kiosk). Then post a job ad here; applicants reply within a day.
Staff work weekdays at your office and are paid every Friday at 17:00, so keep cash in the company.
Morale drops when pay is late or work piles up.

os_contracts.title: Contracts: business deals
lines: Business buyers send offers with quantity, price, delivery date and payment terms.
Accept, counter or decline. Check you can pay for the stock now if they pay you in 60 days.
When a company closes, its undelivered contracts end and its unpaid invoices go to a collector. Old contracts stay visible, but the closed company cannot deliver or collect again.

os_freelance.title: Freelance: consulting for clients
lines: Take a gig from the offers, then work sessions at any laptop. You build the client's spreadsheet yourself by typing it.
Deliver before the deadline for the full fee; late work loses 20% and your reputation. Clients pay on their terms.

os_saas.title: SaaS: build a software product
lines: Pick an idea, then build the first version: code sessions yourself (typing) or hire developers.
Launch when it's ready. Price, ads and new features decide signups and churn; servers cost more as you grow.

business_board.title: The Business Board
lines: Businesses: choose from the businesses available now, or find a part-time job.
Part-time jobs: take one to earn a wage. You work the shifts yourself at the workplace (staff door, press E).
You can run a business and keep a job at the same time.

job.title: Part-time jobs
lines: A shift is 4 hours, one a day, in opening hours. You play the shift: better work pays more (60% of the wage is guaranteed) and earns tips.
Good shifts count toward promotion, and each rank pays more. Every job comes with a perk.

cowork_desk.title: Nexus Co-work
lines: A Day Pass ($15) lets you use the hot desks and their computers today. A monthly desk is cheaper if you come often.

bank.title: Nexus Bank
lines: Open a business account for a registered company, and move money between you and the company.
The teller is open weekdays 9 to 16. Loans are at the manager's desk.

loans.title: Loans
lines: Borrow for stock or a cash gap. You repay monthly with interest; missed payments hurt your credit score.
Check all six lending conditions before signing. A missed condition shows its gap and where to fix it.
Signing takes the afternoon; funds arrive today. First payment in 30 days.

lease.title: Renting an office
lines: An office gives your company desks for staff, more storage and a proper address. Rent is charged every month.

registration.title: Registering a company
lines: Registering costs $300 and turns your business into a company: its own bank account, business contracts, staff.
Choose the name carefully: it goes on your sign and your invoices.

permits.title: Permits
lines: Register as an employer here before you hire staff.
Year 8: importing needs an import licence ($450 a year). A registered company also pays a monthly compliance cost.

packing.title: The packing table
lines: Pack orders by hand: box, padding, tape, label. Poor padding means broken items and returns; a wrong label means late delivery.
Then choose how they leave: book a courier (collects from here for a pickup fee) or carry them to PostPoint yourself.

dropoff.title: PostPoint
lines: Hand over the parcels you're carrying and choose economy (3 days) or express (1 day).

metro.title: The Metro
lines: Pay the fare and pick a station. The ride takes time; walking to a neighbouring district is free.

city_map.title: The city map
lines: Choose an open district to see its location and travel routes.

wardrobe.title: Wardrobe
lines: Change your outfit and accessories. Looks only: clothes never change any numbers. Buy more at Threadline on Shopping Street.

clothing_shop.title: Threadline
lines: Try outfits on the preview, buy with your personal cash, and wear them now or later from your wardrobe.

sleep.title: Your bed
lines: Sleep from 7 PM to end the day; you wake at 7 AM. Time never skips otherwise: work, shop and run the business to fill your days.

decision.title: Decisions
lines: Something happened that needs your call. Each choice has a cost; there is rarely a free option.

month_close.title: Month close
lines: At the start of each month you get last month's report: revenue, costs, profit, and what happened to your cash.

settlement.title: Paying a supplier abroad
lines: In the Clearing Crisis (Year 5), money sent abroad takes days to land, and an importer ships only once it has.
International wire: cheap (1% + $25) but 5 to 9 days.
Letter of credit: Nexus Bank guarantees the payment. 1.5% (at least $60), about 2 days. Needs a business account.
Digital dollars: a licensed exchange sends it in minutes for 0.2% + $1. Needs a verified exchange account (Lina Zhao at Nexus Bank). You carry the platform's risk.
From Year 6 wires clear in 3 to 5 days.
Escrow (Year 6, ask Lina Zhao): your money is locked in a contract and paid to the supplier only when the goods arrive. 0.6% (at least $15), no wire delay, refunded if they never ship.
Each rail shows how often its payments landed on time. A frozen or failed payment lowers it.
Year 8: a payment over $2,500 goes through a KYC check first: a fee and one more day.
A payment stuck on the wire can be switched to a faster rail later: Company OS → Operations → Purchase orders → Speed up.

green_grant.title: Green Business Grant
lines: From Year 4 the city pays a one-off $3,000 grant to registered companies that went green.
You need: recycled packaging (Company OS → Operations) and a green product listed on ShopLane.
Apply at the permits kiosk in City Hall. The money lands in the company account.

os_cafe.title: Café: run a shop, not a warehouse
lines: Customers come from the street: Old Town's foot traffic × how many stop (price and rating) × how many cups the counter can make.
Keep coffee supplies in (they arrive at 6:00 the next morning) and set the daily pastry order; unsold pastries are binned at closing.
Someone must be behind the counter: hire a Barista (People tab), or work the counter yourself inside the café. Walk-outs and running out of coffee pull the rating down.

cafe.title: Your café
lines: Open Mon–Sat 7:00–17:00. The till is banked at closing; card fees are 1.9%.
Work the counter for two hours to open without staff, add a pair of hands when it's busy, and lift the rating with good service.

os_logistics.title: Logistics: a van, runs and thin margins
lines: Runs are posted every morning at 7:00: a client, 4 to 6 stops, a fee and a deadline. Accept one, then drive it: you plan the route on a map.
On time pays the full fee, a shorter route pays a little more, and a late run pays 40% less. A run left undone for hours is cancelled. Fuel and upkeep come off every run.
A Van Driver (People tab) takes one run each workday from 9:00. Your own ecommerce parcels can go out in the van too: choose "Own van" at the packing table.

route_game.title: Plan the route
lines: The van starts at Pier 7, calls at every numbered stop once and comes back. Click the stops in the order you want to drive them.
The river can only be crossed at a bridge. Undo takes the last stop back; the route is drawn as you go.
Your score is the shortest possible route divided by yours. Shorter means less fuel, less time on the road and a little more pay.

purchase_returns.title: Cancel or return a purchase
lines: Operations lists every purchase order, including disabled actions with a reason.

Cancel within the supplier window while the goods are on the way. Unpaid terms reduce accounts payable; any cancellation fee remains due. Unsettled cross-border payments return the principal, but settlement fees stay paid.
For delivered local stock, choose a return quantity up to the unsold and unreserved units at its original location. Pay return freight now; cash arrives after the supplier receives the stock.

Returns normally have a 14-day window, 15% restocking fee, $0.60 freight per unit adjusted by the shipping index, and a 3-day refund delay. Imports accept cancellations only unless the supplier specifies otherwise.

phone_opportunities.title: Opportunities on your phone
lines: Short business stories you can accept from Opportunities on your phone.
Your company and its progress unlock opportunities. Complete the steps to earn contacts; unavailable opportunities end without a reward.

global_markets.title: Overseas markets
lines: Open an international account at Nexus Bank, then use Company OS → Sales → Overseas to open a regional storefront.
Save a price in local currency for each listing. All regions share your stock, so avoid accepting more orders than you can fulfill.
Pack at your existing table and book an international courier. After delivery and the hold period, weekly payouts enter your foreign wallet.
Finance lets you keep foreign currency or convert it now. Automatic conversion runs after weekly payouts. Both choices carry currency risk.

customs.title: Ines explains customs
lines: DDP pays duty before shipping and reduces refusals. DDU leaves duty to the buyer on arrival; refusals are more common.
Choose the actual product category. Correcting a held parcel means duty plus a penalty; documents halve the fine but add 2 days. Withdrawal restores goods, not freight.
The trial needs 10 delivered units with returns below 15%. After two weeks, it needs 5 units; reviewing and pausing expansion is an honest alternative, not a sales success.

city_guide.title: City Guide: find your next stop
lines: Browse buildings by district to see what you can do, opening hours and the nearest Metro station.
Take me there sets the existing gold guide arrow to the building door. Closed buildings still show their hours; you can enter once they open.
Interaction markers show usable spots. Grey markers with a lock explain what you need first. Press I in a room to reopen its introduction.

patch_notes.title: What's new: continuing an older game
lines: This card lists updates after the version that last saved your game. Scroll to read all release notes.
Continue game keeps your progress and records this version so the card does not repeat. New games start with the current version.
Export your save before clearing browser data or switching computers.

os_segments.title: Segments: each business and its shared costs
lines: Revenue, gross profit, expenses and operating profit are shown by business, for this month and last month.
Allocated costs come from common expenses, split by net revenue. Segment totals equal the company report.

manufacturing.title: Line Planner: OEM production
lines: Lease Unit 12, rent a machine and hire Tomas. Fixed costs continue even when the line is idle.
Quote orders, order materials and reserve machine hours within the next week. Changeovers need one hour.
Inspect more to catch defects, or accept refunds and credit risk. Maintenance repairs broken machines.

real_estate.title: Matchmaker and property management
lines: Get the brokerage licence at City Hall, then lease Harlow & Finch. Choose a mandate and a client, compare rooms, budget and urgency, then arrange a viewing.
Mortgages need 20–30% down and run for 20–30 years. Rent and screening affect vacancy; tenants can miss payments or cause damage.
Own a rental before applying for the Lot 7 building permit. Ruiz construction uses paid monthly milestones; unfinished buildings cannot be sold.

media.title: Campaign Mixer: brief to results
lines: Read audience, goal and deadline. Create a pitch, then submit it; losing costs time and money.
Allocate the budget across channels. CPM buys impressions, audience fit and saturation limit relevant reach. Adjust the mix while running.
Daily reports track impressions, clicks and conversions. Finish the scope, then invoice service fees, media rebates and earned KPI bonuses.

creative_pitch.title: Creative Pitch: read the client preferences
lines: Choose a slogan, visual and tone. The brief and university mentor explain the audience preferences.
Matching cards improves creative quality and click-through; cheap interns assist more slowly than designers.

hotel.title: Rate Board: price, channels, rooms
lines: Take over or lease the Aster Inn, then set prices per room type against the 30-day demand calendar.
Direct guests pay no commission, the OTA brings volume for 15% to 18%, and agency blocks lock rooms at 25% off weeks ahead.
Housekeepers decide how many rooms can be sold. Reviews of cleanliness, service and value drive your OTA ranking and demand.

energy.title: Energy Console: roof to charging network
lines: Survey a roof, place panels around shade and the load limit, then send a quote with or without a subsidy.
Order materials from Helio Supply, then crew-days finish the install. Rain slows work and storms stop it.
With storage certification and two installs you can build charging stations. Set a price per kWh and watch demand.

automotive.title: Auto Desk: auction, fleet, showroom
lines: Auction: inspect lots before Wednesday, bid live on auction day, then recondition and list the car. A higher price means more days to sell.
Rental fleet: lease the Gateway counter, buy cars, set day and week rates and schedule services. Skipped service causes breakdowns mid-rental.
Dealership: build a ten-car fleet and 25 rentals, lease the showroom, pay the deposit and keep new cars in stock.

os_automotive.title: Auto Desk: auction, fleet, showroom
lines: Auction: inspect lots before Wednesday, bid live on auction day, then recondition and list the car. A higher price means more days to sell.
Rental fleet: lease the Gateway counter, buy cars, set day and week rates and schedule services. Skipped service causes breakdowns mid-rental.
Dealership: build a ten-car fleet and 25 rentals, lease the showroom, pay the deposit and keep new cars in stock.

auction.title: Auction: bid before the hammer falls
lines: Press Bid to raise by one step. Bidders raise until they reach private limits; after a few quiet ticks the hammer falls.
The buyer fee is added to the price. Stop bidding when the price passes what the car is worth to you.

os_group.title: Group: trade between your businesses
lines: Set a transfer price for each running pair: at cost, cost plus a markup or market price. Both businesses show the trade in Segments.
Group totals eliminate internal trade, so moving money between your own businesses never makes the group richer or poorer; only real savings do.
Group jobs are big orders that need two or more industries. Unfinished parts can be subcontracted for a fee.

industry_first_order.title: First industry order
lines: This optional guide follows real industry work. Close it to operate in Company OS, then reopen the industry tab for the next step.
Already completed work is skipped. Skip this guide hides the coaching; your accepted phone opportunity keeps its own progress.
